newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japanese coffee roasters still mulling price rise.
newsitem.headline: Japanese coffee roasters still mulling price rise.

text.p: Japan"s coffee roasters are facing mounting pressure to raise retail prices, as the yen"s weakness and surging global coffee prices erode their profit margins, industry sources said on Wednesday.
"The circumstances we are facing are even tougher than when coffee prices surged in early 1995 due to frosts in Brazil," an official at a major roaster said.
After the 1995 rally, Japan"s retail prices for instant coffee were raised by an average of 12 percent.
The official suggested a double-digit price increase was possible again this year, although it was still too early to tell.

Industry sources noted that while some Japanese coffee roasters had already started talks with end-users on retail price hikes, others were still monitoring world prices and exchange rates before making a decision.

Coffee prices on New York"s Coffee, Sugar and Cocoa Exchange have rallied more than 60 percent in the past two months, with the most active May futures contract reaching 172.25 cents a lb last Friday, only 15 cents short of highs hit during the frost-inspired rally two years ago.

Prices tumbled on Tuesday to 157.25 cents a lb as a strike in Colombia ended, but traders attributed this to an overdue correction after the spectacular run-up and insisted that the market"s bullish fundamentals remained intact.

"Backed by dwindling world coffee stocks and expectations that the Brazilian crop for 1997/98 will be lower, I don"t see much scope for global coffee prices to fall in the near term," a trader at a major trading house said.
Also boosting yen-based prices for Japanese roasters is the yen"s steep fall against the dollar in recent months to its lowest levels in four years.
The higher prices have made Japanese traders cautious about buying in the global market, leading to a further decline in domestic coffee stocks.

Japan"s warehouse stocks of coffee have been in a steady downtrend since last year"s peak in September of 65,351 tonnes, according to data from the Agriculture Ministry. At the end of December, stocks totalled 58,696 tonnes.
